factual_claims.claim: Despite higher leverage, liquidity remained solid with cash balances growing to €11.29 million and trade receivable collectability maintaining a high ninety-nine-point-sixty-eight percent rate.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED

factual_claims.claim: A statutory obligation to harmonize water prices for private and business customers drove an eighteen-point-three percent surge in private customer sales, offsetting a two-point-seven percent decline in commercial billing.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The SALES section states sales to private customers increased by 18.3% to €31.84 million, while sales to business customers decreased by 2.7% to €16.76 million, citing tariff harmonization as the cause.

factual_claims.claim: Additionally, a regulatory pricing reform redirected combined sewer revenues into wastewater collection lines, structurally altering segment reporting.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The SALES FROM THE OPERATION... section explains that from 1 July 2024, revenue from the combined sewer system is now reflected in wastewater collection and treatment services, changing segment reporting.

factual_claims.claim: Throughout the period, the organization maintained uninterrupted service delivery, successfully managing infrastructure upgrades and meeting established operational continuity targets without material disruptions.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The MANAGEMENT REPORT highlights continuity of vital water services, successful crisis plan testing during frazil ice events, and notes that 'the number of blockages decreased by 18% in 2025, while the number of water emergencies fell by 23%.'
